sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Douglas County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Douglas County splits property tax between the Appraisal Department, which values property, and the elected Tax Commissioner, who bills and collects. The Appraisal Department works for the Board of Assessors and takes appeals. The Tax Commissioner's office also takes homestead applications, and its website covers the tax bill, assessment notices, exemptions, delinquent taxes and tax sales.

  • Appraisal Department: mailing address 8700 Hospital Dr., Douglasville, GA 30134, phone 770-920-7228. In-person filing happens on the second floor of the county annex at 6200 Fairburn Rd.
  • Tax Commissioner: first floor of the Douglas County Government Annex, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and closed from noon to 1:00 p.m.
  • Finance Department: posts the millage rate documents and public hearing schedule. The 2026 set was revised as of September 4.

Appraisal staff also walk the county. Under O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1 they check building permit status and review new construction, additions, remodels, sales and appeals, and they photograph and measure properties. They carry a photo badge and drive a marked vehicle.

sections.h2: When were Douglas County's 2026 assessment notices mailed and when did appeals close?
sections.html:
The county mailed 2026 annual assessment notices on June 16, 2026, and the deadline to appeal was July 31, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. That deadline has passed. The Appraisal Department states plainly that it cannot extend the filing date, so it asks owners to file early and keep a copy.

The notices arrive between April 15 and July 1 in a normal cycle, and you have 45 days from the date on the notice. Appeals can be filed by mail, in person or online, with a dropbox in the annex parking lot for after hours. The county does not accept appeals by fax or email. Anyone filing for an owner needs to attach a letter of authorization.

Before you appeal, ask for the property record card and the comparable sales on file at the Appraisal Department. Personal property owners get a notice only if the value changes or the county disagrees with a return filed between January 1 and April 1.

sections.h2: How does a Douglas County appeal move from the assessors to court?
sections.html:
It moves in steps, and you can stop at any of them if you accept the number. The standard path runs through the Board of Equalization, a panel appointed by the grand jury.

  1. The Board of Assessors reviews the value and sends a written letter, called the 30-day letter, saying whether it changed anything.
  2. If the value stands, the appeal goes straight to the Board of Equalization. If the value dropped and you accept it, the appeal ends when the 30 days run out.
  3. If you reject a changed value, tell the Appraisal Department in writing inside the 30 days so the file moves on.
  4. The Board of Equalization mails a hearing date. The county recommends that you attend with your own evidence of market value.
  5. Either side may take the decision to Superior Court within 30 days of its mailing, with a $25 filing fee paid to the Clerk of Superior Court.

At the time you file you may choose a different route. Arbitration covers value only. A hearing officer takes a non-homestead parcel with a fair market value above $500,000, limited to value and uniformity. A direct Superior Court appeal needs the Board of Assessors' consent and allows any ground. The Georgia Department of Revenue confirms that an appeal can rest on taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions can Douglas County owners claim?
sections.html:
An owner who lived in the home on January 1 can apply to the Tax Commissioner by April 1, online or in person, and the county accepts applications year-round for the following cycle. You need a state ID or driver's license plus a motor vehicle registration showing the homestead address. The Revenue Department adds that a homestead application may also be filed during the 45-day appeal window.

The county's exemption page lists these categories:

  • Standard homestead exemption.
  • Senior exemptions at 62 and at 65, with a separate 65 fixed-income version that has an income test.
  • Disability, backed by two forms of proof or two doctors' certificates, plus a letter from the Social Security Administration.
  • Disabled veteran, with a VA statement of 100 percent service-connected benefits as of January 1.
  • Surviving spouse of someone killed in action or of a police officer or firefighter killed in the line of duty.

The Revenue Department also names Douglas County among the counties with a base-year valuation freeze exemption, which fixes the taxable value at an earlier year for as long as the owner lives there. Ask the Tax Commissioner for the base year and any qualifying rules.

sections.h2: What do Douglas County's housing numbers show?
sections.html:
Douglas County is a growing county with 200 square miles of land and about 720 people per square mile. Its population estimate for July 1, 2025 was 154,293, up 6.9 percent from the 2020 base, and the Census Bureau counted 801 building permits for 2025. Workers report a mean trip of 33.2 minutes to their jobs.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work when you sell a house in Douglas County?
sections.html:
The person who owned the property on January 1 is responsible for that year's tax, and Georgia does not refund part of a year to someone who sells. The Revenue Department says a bill generally allows 60 days to pay, with most counties using December 20 as the due date. Ask the Douglas County Tax Commissioner for the exact bill date and balance on your parcel.

The Tax Commissioner's website lists delinquent taxes, upcoming tax sales and an excess funds list, so it is the place to check for any unpaid prior year. County tax liens are filed in the clerk's office on the general execution docket, and the commissioner can tell you whether one exists against your parcel.

If you plan to split a lot before selling, start with a survey and take it to the Zoning Administrator for approval. After the stamped survey is recorded, you sign new deeds and record them with the Clerk of Superior Court, and the Appraisal Department has a deed specialist who handles those changes on the tax side. Sellers with an inherited or behind-on-taxes house in Douglas County often choose an as-is sale to a cash buyer so the taxes clear at closing without repairs.

faqs.q: Did Douglas County really close appeals on July 31, 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. The county mailed 2026 notices on June 16 and set July 31, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. as the deadline. It states it cannot extend the date, so that window is over and the next notices will bring a new 45-day period.

faqs.q: Can I appeal a Douglas County assessment by email?
faqs.a: No. The Appraisal Department accepts appeals by mail, in person at the annex, or online through the property search links. Fax and email are not accepted, and a representative must include a letter of authorization.

faqs.q: What does a Douglas County Superior Court appeal cost?
faqs.a: The filing fee is $25, paid to the Clerk of Superior Court, and you must notify the assessors in writing. Either the owner or the Board of Assessors may appeal a Board of Equalization decision within 30 days of its mailing.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for a Douglas County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Apply with the Douglas County Tax Commissioner, online or in person, with a state ID or driver's license and vehicle registration at the home address. You must have owned and lived in the house on January 1, and April 1 is the usual filing deadline.

faqs.q: Who owes the property tax if I sell my Douglas County house in the spring?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner owes the whole year, and Georgia gives no partial-year refund. The sale contract and closing statement decide how it is split, so request a balance from the Tax Commissioner first.
